records.context: The warm-up polishes before it shows. Qt posts every new widget a ``PolishRequest``, and a dialog built ahead in an idle slice (:func:`_warm_the_preferences`) answers it in the next pass of the event loop, long before :meth:`setVisible`. The window sheet and the glass then walked all ~967 widgets of every tab in that one event: 425-484 ms offscreen, 0.36 s on the lesson capture host. The pages leave here as they would at the show, and the polish styles the open tab only.
records.label: spacr.qt.preferences._preferences_window_class._PreferencesWindow.event#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: THE WARM-UP POLISHES BEFORE IT SHOWS. Qt posts every new widget a ``PolishRequest``, and a dialog built ahead in an idle slice (:func:`_warm_the_preferences`) answers it in the next pass of the event loop, long before :meth:`setVisible`. The window sheet and the glass then walked all ~967 widgets of every tab in that one event: 425-484 ms offscreen, 0.36 s on the lesson capture host. The pages leave here as they would at the show, and the polish styles the open tab only.
records.translation: El precalentamiento pule antes de que se muestre. Qt envía a cada widget nuevo un ``PolishRequest``, y un diálogo construido de antemano en un intervalo inactivo (:func:`_warm_the_preferences`) lo responde en la siguiente pasada del bucle de eventos, mucho antes de :meth:`setVisible`. La hoja de estilo de la ventana y el efecto de cristal recorrían entonces los ~967 widgets de todas las pestañas en ese único evento: 425-484 ms fuera de pantalla, 0.36 s en el equipo de captura de las lecciones. Las páginas salen de aquí como lo harían al mostrarse, y el pulido aplica estilo solo a la pestaña abierta.

records.context: Only for a dialog the warm-up built, which says so through ``_pages_leave_at_the_polish``. Anything else that builds the dialog and lets the event loop run before walking a page -- the help search index reads every tab's form rows that way -- still finds every page where the builder put it until the show.
records.label: spacr.qt.preferences._preferences_window_class._PreferencesWindow.event#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ONLY FOR A DIALOG THE WARM-UP BUILT, which says so through ``_pages_leave_at_the_polish``. Anything else that builds the dialog and lets the event loop run before walking a page -- the help search index reads every tab's form rows that way -- still finds every page where the builder put it until the show.
records.translation: Solo para un diálogo que construyó el precalentamiento, que lo indica mediante ``_pages_leave_at_the_polish``. Cualquier otra cosa que construya el diálogo y deje correr el bucle de eventos antes de recorrer una página -- el índice de búsqueda de la ayuda lee así las filas de formulario de cada pestaña -- sigue encontrando cada página donde la puso el constructor hasta que se muestra.

records.context: The user's explicit ask was a toggle that works *now*, so this walks the running widget tree the same way :func:`spacr.qt.button_roles.install_button_roles` does and updates the widgets in place instead of waiting for the application views to be rebuilt. records.source: The user's explicit ask was a toggle that works *now*, so this walks the running widget tree the same way :func:`spacr.qt.button_roles.install_button_roles` does and updates the widgets in place instead of waiting for the screens to be rebuilt. Hiding one also stops its timer (the widget stops animating whenever it is not visible), so "off" really is zero frames.
records.translation: Lo que pidió explícitamente el usuario fue un conmutador que funcione *ya*, así que esto recorre el árbol de widgets en ejecución igual que :func:`spacr.qt.button_roles.install_button_roles` y actualiza los widgets in situ en lugar de esperar a que se reconstruyan las pantallas. Ocultar uno también detiene su temporizador (el widget deja de animarse siempre que no es visible), de modo que "off" (desactivado) significa realmente cero fotogramas.

records.source: Answers ``False`` outright when ``SPACR_NO_BACKDROP`` is set, whatever is stored. `spacr.qt.crash_recovery` sets it after spaCR has died on launch twice running: the backdrop is the only thing spaCR asks a driver to do at startup, and the setting that would turn it off is behind the window that never appears. records.translation: Responde ``False`` sin más cuando ``SPACR_NO_BACKDROP`` está definida, sea cual sea el valor guardado. `spacr.qt.crash_recovery` la define después de que spaCR haya fallado al arrancar dos veces seguidas: el fondo es lo único que spaCR pide a un controlador al arrancar, y el ajuste que lo desactivaría está detrás de la ventana que nunca aparece. Es local al proceso y nunca se guarda, de modo que la siguiente ejecución limpia lo restaura sin que el usuario tenga que deshacer nada.

records.source: Default ``True``. When this is ``False`` no ambient widget should be installed at all — and any already-installed one is hidden and stopped by :func:`apply_ambient_preferences`, so the toggle takes effect the moment Preferences is saved rather than at the next launch.
records.translation: Por defecto, ``True``. Cuando es ``False`` no debería instalarse ningún widget de ambiente — y cualquiera ya instalado lo oculta y detiene :func:`apply_ambient_preferences`, de modo que el conmutador surte efecto en cuanto se guarda Preferences y no en el siguiente arranque.

records.context: **Two keys answer this one question, and both are honoured.** The Animation preference gained a ``None`` entry (see :data:`spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.NO_ANIMATION`), and "no animation" has to mean *nothing is constructed* rather than "an engine that paints an empty frame sixty times a second". The three install sites all read this function before they build anything, so answering ``False`` for None here is what makes the guarantee true everywhere at once, without a second condition in three other modules that could drift apart.
records.label: spacr.qt.preferences.get_ambient_enabled#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Two keys answer this one question, and both are honoured.** The Animation preference gained a ``None`` entry (see :data:`spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.NO_ANIMATION`), and "no animation" has to mean *nothing is constructed* rather than "an engine that paints an empty frame sixty times a second". The three install sites all read this function before they build anything, so answering ``False`` for None here is what makes the guarantee true everywhere at once, without a second condition in three other modules that could drift apart.
records.translation: **Dos claves responden a esta única pregunta, y se respetan ambas.** La preferencia Animation incorporó una entrada ``None`` (véase :data:`spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.NO_ANIMATION`), y "no animation" (sin animación) tiene que significar que *no se construye nada*, y no "an engine that paints an empty frame sixty times a second" (un motor que pinta un fotograma vacío sesenta veces por segundo). Los tres puntos de instalación leen esta función antes de construir nada, así que responder ``False`` aquí para None es lo que hace que la garantía se cumpla en todas partes a la vez, sin una segunda condición en otros tres módulos que podrían divergir.

records.source: Read by :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png`, which is the single consumer. ``pdf`` makes it write a vector page beside the display raster; the queue then rasterises that page for a crisper view and the user has a file that opens as editable art. Scope is worth stating, since the name suggests otherwise: this is the format of the figures spaCR renders **for its own Figures panel**. Figures a pipeline writes into a results directory are saved by ``savefig`` calls in :mod:`spacr.plot`, :mod:`spacr.submodules`, :mod:`spacr.ml` and friends, each of which hard-codes its own format and never reads this preference.
records.translation: Lo lee :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png`, que es su único consumidor. ``pdf`` hace que escriba una página vectorial junto al ráster de pantalla; la cola rasteriza después esa página para una vista más nítida, y el usuario obtiene un archivo que se abre como gráfico editable. Conviene precisar el alcance, ya que el nombre sugiere otra cosa: es el formato de las figuras que spaCR representa **para su propio panel Figures**. Las figuras que un pipeline escribe en un directorio de resultados las guardan llamadas a ``savefig`` en :mod:`spacr.plot`, :mod:`spacr.submodules`, :mod:`spacr.ml` y similares, cada una de las cuales fija su propio formato en el código y nunca lee esta preferencia.

records.context: Two consumers, and they treat it differently on purpose. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png` clamps it for the on-application view raster — a 16x12" figure at 300 DPI is a 4800 px PNG that costs more to decode than any application view can show — so a large figure is displayed at a lower DPI than the one chosen here. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue._export_vector_pdf` uses the value unclamped, because the PDF is a file rather than a screenful and its embedded rasters really do need the resolution the user asked for.

records.translation: Dos consumidores, que la tratan de forma distinta a propósito. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png` la limita para el ráster en pantalla — una figura de 16x12" a 300 DPI es un PNG de 4800 px que cuesta más decodificar de lo que ninguna pantalla puede mostrar —, de modo que una figura grande se muestra con menos DPI que los elegidos aquí. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue._export_vector_pdf` usa el valor sin limitar, porque el PDF es un archivo y no una pantalla, y sus rásteres incrustados necesitan de verdad la resolución que pidió el usuario.

records.context: Whether setting tooltips show their animation WITHOUT being asked.

records.source: Whether setting tooltips show their animation WITHOUT being asked.
records.translation: Si los tooltips de los ajustes muestran su animación SIN que se les pida.

records.context: Default ``False``: a hover is text only, no GIF is decoded, no frames are cached and no timer runs, and the teal **Animation** word in the footer is the invitation to see one — for that setting, once. Turning this on starts every tooltip revealed instead, and the word then folds the one in front of the reader away. The meaning is "stop asking me", not "allow animations".
records.label: spacr.qt.preferences.get_setting_animations_enabled#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Default ``False``: a hover is text only, no GIF is decoded, no frames are cached and no timer runs, and the teal **Animation** word in the footer is the invitation to see one — for that setting, once. Turning this on starts every tooltip revealed instead, and the word then folds the one in front of the reader away. The meaning is "stop asking me", not "allow animations".
records.translation: Por defecto, ``False``: un paso del cursor muestra solo texto, no se decodifica ningún GIF, no se guarda ningún fotograma en caché y no corre ningún temporizador, y la palabra **Animation** en verde azulado del pie es la invitación a ver una — para ese ajuste, una vez. Activar esto hace que todos los tooltips empiecen mostrándola, y entonces la palabra pliega la que tiene delante el lector. El significado es "stop asking me" (deja de preguntarme), no "allow animations" (permitir animaciones).

records.translation: Un UPDATE sobre ``measurements.db`` es irrecuperable, así que cada una de las protecciones siguientes tiene que fallar hacia la *solo lectura*:

records.context: 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` must be on — it is off by default and lives in Preferences, not on this screen. 2. The database must have been chosen explicitly in this session (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``). 3. The user must tick "Edit mode" *and* confirm; ticking alone does nothing. 4. The row must be addressable by ``rowid`` or a primary structured-data name. Without one, the edit is refused — an UPDATE matching on column values can hit many rows, which on a measurements table is silent mass corruption. The write also probes ``COUNT(*)`` for the row address first and rolls back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The typed text must be coercible to the column's declared type. SQLite stores ``'abc'`` in an INTEGER column without error; :func:`coerce_for_column` refuses instead.

records.source: 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` must be on — it is off by default and lives in Preferences, not on this screen. 2. The database must have been chosen explicitly in this session (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``). 3. The user must tick "Edit mode" *and* confirm; ticking alone does nothing. 4. The row must be addressable by ``rowid`` or a primary key. Without one, the edit is refused — an UPDATE matching on column values can hit many rows, which on a measurements table is silent mass corruption. The write also probes ``COUNT(*)`` for the row address first and rolls back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The typed text must be coercible to the column's declared type. SQLite stores ``'abc'`` in an INTEGER column without error; :func:`coerce_for_column` refuses instead.
records.translation: 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` debe estar activada — está desactivada por defecto y se encuentra en Preferences, no en esta pantalla. 2. La base de datos debe haberse elegido explícitamente en esta sesión (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``). 3. El usuario debe marcar "Edit mode" (modo de edición) *y* confirmar; marcarlo sin más no hace nada. 4. La fila debe poder direccionarse por ``rowid`` o por una clave primaria. Sin ninguna, la edición se rechaza — un UPDATE que coincida por valores de columna puede afectar a muchas filas, lo que en una tabla de mediciones es una corrupción masiva silenciosa. Además, la escritura comprueba primero ``COUNT(*)`` para la dirección de la fila y revierte salvo que ``rowcount == 1``. 5. El texto tecleado debe poder convertirse al tipo declarado de la columna. SQLite guarda ``'abc'`` en una columna INTEGER sin error; :func:`coerce_for_column`, en cambio, lo rechaza.

records.context: Design notes that matter for real spaCR databases:
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Design notes that matter for real spaCR databases:
records.translation: Notas de diseño relevantes para bases de datos reales de spaCR:

records.context: Never ``SELECT *`` the whole table. Measurement tables run to hundreds of thousands of rows and hundreds of feature columns. The first chunk (100 rows) is fetched and painted on its own; the rest arrives as the user scrolls, through ``canFetchMore`` / ``fetchMore``.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Never ``SELECT *`` the whole table. Measurement tables run to hundreds of thousands of rows and hundreds of feature columns. The first chunk (100 rows) is fetched and painted on its own; the rest arrives as the user scrolls, through ``canFetchMore`` / ``fetchMore``.
records.translation: Nunca se hace ``SELECT *`` de la tabla entera. Las tablas de mediciones llegan a cientos de miles de filas y cientos de columnas de características. El primer bloque (100 filas) se obtiene y se pinta por separado; el resto llega a medida que el usuario se desplaza, mediante ``canFetchMore`` / ``fetchMore``.

records.context: **Keyset paging, not OFFSET.** Each chunk asks for ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` and ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` makes SQLite walk (and throw away) every skipped row, so chunk 500 of a 400 k-row table would cost 500× chunk 1. Only tables with no usable structured-data name (views, composite-primary-structured-data name ``WITHOUT ROWID`` tables) fall back to ``OFFSET``, and those are small by construction.

records.source: **Keyset paging, not OFFSET.** Each chunk asks for ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` and ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` makes SQLite walk (and throw away) every skipped row, so chunk 500 of a 400 k-row table would cost 500× chunk 1. records.translation: **El recuento nunca bloquea el primer pintado.** ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` es un recorrido completo. El primer bloque se pinta frente a ``max(rowid)``, que es O(1), y ese número se muestra *siempre* como "≈… (estimate)" (estimación). records.context: **Cancellable.** Switching table or database bumps a load token. Results tagged with a stale token are dropped, so an in-flight load can never paint the previous table's rows into the new view, and a job that has not started yet is dropped without spending an independent execution path. Nothing is ever killed mid-flight.

records.source: **Cancellable.** Switching table or database bumps a load token. Results tagged with a stale token are dropped, so an in-flight load can never paint the previous table's rows into the new view, and a job that has not started yet is dropped without spending a thread. records.context: **Incremental fetch.** ``canFetchMore``/``fetchMore`` are Qt's incremental-loading interface; the view calls them when the user scrolls to the bottom and the model asks the application view for another chunk. While a chunk is in flight ``canFetchMore`` is False, so a scroll cannot schedule ten of them.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser.PreviewModel#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Incremental fetch.** ``canFetchMore``/``fetchMore`` are Qt's incremental-loading interface; the view calls them when the user scrolls to the bottom and the model asks the screen for another chunk. While a chunk is in flight ``canFetchMore`` is False, so a scroll cannot queue ten of them.
records.translation: **Obtención incremental.** ``canFetchMore``/``fetchMore`` son la interfaz de carga incremental de Qt; la vista las llama cuando el usuario se desplaza hasta abajo y el modelo pide otro bloque a la pantalla. Mientras hay un bloque en curso, ``canFetchMore`` es False, de modo que un desplazamiento no puede poner diez en cola.

records.context: **Row identity.** Every row carries the structured-data name tuple it was fetched with (``rowid``, or the primary structured-data name). That is what makes an edit addressable — and its absence is what makes an edit refusable.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser.PreviewModel#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Row identity.** Every row carries the key tuple it was fetched with (``rowid``, or the primary key). That is what makes an edit addressable — and its absence is what makes an edit refusable.
records.translation: **Identidad de fila.** Cada fila lleva la tupla de clave con la que se obtuvo (``rowid`` o la clave primaria). Eso es lo que hace direccionable una edición — y su ausencia es lo que permite rechazarla.

records.context: paging falls back to ``OFFSET``. records.context: **Brush** and **Erase** paint and unpaint the active label a pixel at a time. **Erase object** removes a whole label in one click. **Wand** grows a region from the pixel clicked and adds it to the mask by default. Hold Ctrl while clicking to remove that region; the tolerance is relative to the image's intensity range by default, see :func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.relative_tolerance`. **Draw** traces a free-form outline that closes and fills as ONE object -- the tool a brush is not, because a brush stamps disks along the path, so tracing a rim with it labels the rim and leaves the middle background. **Divide / Merge** uses a left-button drag to divide and a right-button drag to merge crossed objects under the first touched identifier without changing their pixels. The merged identity is retained when saving and reopening. Dividing drags a line across a merged object and makes it two, keeping the original identifier on the larger component and giving the smaller a new one, with every other object untouched; :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.DIVIDE_CUT_WIDTH` is the cut width. **Zoom** rectangle-drags the view and changes no labels at all.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.make_masks#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Brush** and **Erase** paint and unpaint the active label a pixel at a time. **Erase object** removes a whole label in one click. **Wand** grows a region from the pixel clicked and adds it to the mask by default. Hold Ctrl while clicking to remove that region; the tolerance is relative to the image's intensity range by default, see :func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.relative_tolerance`. **Draw** traces a free-form outline that closes and fills as ONE object -- the tool a brush is not, because a brush stamps disks along the path, so tracing a rim with it labels the rim and leaves the middle background. **Divide / Merge** uses a left-button drag to divide and a right-button drag to merge crossed objects under the first touched identifier without changing their pixels. The merged identity is retained when saving and reopening. Dividing drags a line across a merged object and makes it two, keeping the original identifier on the larger component and giving the smaller a new one, with every other object untouched; :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.DIVIDE_CUT_WIDTH` is the cut width. **Zoom** rectangle-drags the view and changes no labels at all.
records.translation: **Brush** y **Erase** pintan y despintan la etiqueta activa píxel a píxel. **Erase object** elimina una etiqueta entera con un clic. **Wand** hace crecer una región a partir del píxel pulsado y, por defecto, la añade a la máscara. Mantenga pulsado Ctrl al hacer clic para eliminar esa región; por defecto, la tolerancia es relativa al rango de intensidad de la imagen, véase :func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.relative_tolerance`. **Draw** traza un contorno a mano alzada que se cierra y se rellena como UN ÚNICO objeto -- la herramienta que no es un pincel, porque un pincel estampa discos a lo largo del trazo, de modo que repasar un borde con él etiqueta el borde y deja el interior como fondo. **Divide / Merge** usa un arrastre con el botón izquierdo para dividir y uno con el botón derecho para fusionar los objetos atravesados bajo el identificador del primero tocado, sin cambiar sus píxeles. La identidad fusionada se conserva al guardar y volver a abrir. Dividir arrastra una línea a través de un objeto fusionado y lo convierte en dos, conservando el identificador original en el componente mayor y dando uno nuevo al menor, sin tocar ningún otro objeto; :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.DIVIDE_CUT_WIDTH` es la anchura del corte. **Zoom** amplía la vista arrastrando un rectángulo y no cambia ninguna etiqueta.

records.context: ``_MaskLoadWorker`` is parented to this widget, so without this the application view's destructor deletes a QThread that is still decoding a large TIFF, and Qt answers that with ``qFatal("QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running")`` — a core dump, not an exception. The window is exactly as wide as one image decode, which is why it shows up in a loaded test shard and almost never by hand.

records.source: ``_MaskLoadWorker`` is parented to this widget, so without this the screen's destructor deletes a QThread that is still decoding a large TIFF, and Qt answers that with ``qFatal("QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running")`` — a core dump, not an exception. The window is exactly as wide as one image decode, which is why it shows up in a loaded test shard and almost never by hand.
records.translation: ``_MaskLoadWorker`` tiene como padre este widget, así que sin esto el destructor de la pantalla elimina un QThread que todavía está decodificando un TIFF grande, y Qt responde con ``qFatal("QThread: Destroyed while thread is still running")`` — un volcado de memoria, no una excepción. La ventana de riesgo dura exactamente lo que una decodificación de imagen, y por eso aparece en un fragmento de pruebas cargado y casi nunca a mano.

records.context: Closing the panel is not enough. A module polls the machine's RAM and GPU on a background execution unit, and Qt answers an executing QThread being destroyed by aborting the process — so the module's own close handler, which drains that worker, has to execute. A page nested inside another module's tabs never gets one from Qt, which is why they are closed by hand here.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.make_masks.MakeMasksScreen.close_folded#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Closing the panel is not enough. A module polls the machine's RAM and GPU on a worker thread, and Qt answers a running QThread being destroyed by aborting the process — so the module's own close handler, which drains that worker, has to run. A page nested inside another module's tabs never gets one from Qt, which is why they are closed by hand here.
records.translation: Cerrar el panel no basta. Un módulo consulta la RAM y la GPU de la máquina en un hilo worker, y Qt responde a la destrucción de un QThread en ejecución abortando el proceso — así que debe ejecutarse el manejador de cierre propio del módulo, que vacía ese worker. Una página anidada dentro de las pestañas de otro módulo nunca recibe uno de Qt, y por eso aquí se cierran a mano.

records.context: Every module that was built, not every module that was opened. A module is built the moment something asks this application view to point it at the open folder — :meth:`seed_folded` does, and so does any test or caller reaching for :meth:`folded_screen` — and pointing Model Compare at a folder starts a load independent execution path before its panel has ever been on application view. Walking the panels alone left those independent execution paths executing with nothing holding them, and the process died of it several actions later, in whatever happened to be executing when the memory behind them was touched.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.make_masks.MakeMasksScreen.close_folded#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: EVERY MODULE THAT WAS BUILT, not every module that was opened. A module is built the moment something asks this screen to point it at the open folder — :meth:`seed_folded` does, and so does any test or caller reaching for :meth:`folded_screen` — and pointing Model Compare at a folder starts a load thread before its panel has ever been on screen. Walking the panels alone left those threads running with nothing holding them, and the process died of it several actions later, in whatever happened to be running when the memory behind them was touched.
records.translation: Todos los módulos que se construyeron, no todos los que se abrieron. Un módulo se construye en cuanto algo pide a esta pantalla que lo apunte a la carpeta abierta — lo hace :meth:`seed_folded`, y también cualquier prueba o llamador que recurra a :meth:`folded_screen` —, y apuntar Model Compare a una carpeta inicia un hilo de carga antes de que su panel haya estado nunca en pantalla. Recorrer solo los paneles dejaba esos hilos en marcha sin nada que los retuviera, y el proceso moría por ello varias acciones después, en lo que estuviera ejecutándose cuando se tocaba la memoria que había detrás.

records.source: The image goes in as a **batch of one**, which is what :func:`spacr.spacr_cellpose.parse_cellpose4_output` — the repository's own reader of this return value — is written for. Handed a bare 2-D array instead, ``eval`` returns a flat three-member flows list and that function reads ``len(masks)`` as the number of images and finds the image height, so the parse fails on an image that segmented perfectly well.
records.translation: La imagen entra como un **lote de una**, que es para lo que está escrita :func:`spacr.spacr_cellpose.parse_cellpose4_output` — el lector propio del repositorio de este valor devuelto. records.translation: Un ``QMessageBox`` modal ejecuta su propio bucle de eventos y solo devuelve cuando alguien pulsa un botón. records.context: The probability map runs roughly -12..+8 and the flow components ±5; the intensity image is 16-bit counts. Shown raw beside each other they are three different scales and none of them is readable. records.source: The probability map runs roughly -12..+8 and the flow components ±5; the intensity image is 16-bit counts. Stretching each one by its own percentiles is what puts them on the same footing as the contrast-stretched intensity image the canvas already draws, which is the only way the panes can be compared with it by eye.
records.translation: El mapa de probabilidad va aproximadamente de -12..+8 y los componentes del flujo de ±5; la imagen de intensidad son recuentos de 16 bits. Mostrados en bruto uno junto a otro son tres escalas distintas y ninguna es legible. Estirar cada uno por sus propios percentiles es lo que los pone al mismo nivel que la imagen de intensidad con contraste estirado que ya dibuja el lienzo, que es la única forma de compararlos con ella a simple vista.

records.context: Newer releases are then added. The wheel for a release cannot contain its own release note -- the note is written when the GitHub release is published, which is after that wheel is on PyPI -- so a bundled file is always one release behind the build carrying it. After the page is shown, :attr:`refresh_requested` asks the window to read the public releases list on a background execution unit, and :meth:`apply_releases` merges whatever comes back in front of the bundled list. Nothing here opens a socket: the panel only asks, and a fetch that fails, is rate-limited, is switched off in Preferences, or simply finds nothing newer leaves the bundled list exactly as it was drawn.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.home.NewsPanel#2

records.source: Newer releases are then added. The wheel for a release cannot contain its own release note -- the note is written when the GitHub release is published, which is after that wheel is on PyPI -- so a bundled file is always one release behind the build carrying it. After the page is shown, :attr:`refresh_requested` asks the window to read the public releases list on a worker thread, and :meth:`apply_releases` merges whatever comes back in front of the bundled list. Nothing here opens a socket: the panel only asks, and a fetch that fails, is rate-limited, is switched off in Preferences, or simply finds nothing newer leaves the bundled list exactly as it was drawn.
records.translation: Después se añaden las versiones más recientes. El wheel de una versión no puede contener su propia nota de versión -- la nota se escribe cuando se publica la versión en GitHub, que es después de que ese wheel esté en PyPI --, así que un archivo incluido siempre va una versión por detrás de la compilación que lo contiene. Una vez mostrada la página, :attr:`refresh_requested` pide a la ventana que lea la lista pública de versiones en un hilo worker, y :meth:`apply_releases` fusiona lo que llegue delante de la lista incluida. Aquí no se abre ningún socket: el panel solo lo pide, y una descarga que falla, está limitada por tasa, está desactivada en Preferences o simplemente no encuentra nada más nuevo deja la lista incluida exactamente como se dibujó.

Release bodies are GitHub-flavoured markdown; what they contain in practice is bullet lists, bare URLs and ``**bold**``, and a QLabel understands a handful of tags. records.source: This is not a Markdown renderer. Release bodies are GitHub-flavoured markdown; what they contain in practice is bullet lists, bare URLs and ``**bold**``, and a QLabel understands a handful of tags. So: escape everything first -- a body is text from a web page and must never reach a rich-text widget as markup -- then put back the three constructs that are worth having.
records.translation: No es un renderizador de Markdown. Los cuerpos de las versiones están en markdown al estilo de GitHub; lo que contienen en la práctica son listas con viñetas, URLs sueltas y ``**bold**``, y un QLabel entiende un puñado de etiquetas. Así que: primero se escapa todo -- un cuerpo es texto de una página web y nunca debe llegar como marcado a un widget de texto enriquecido -- y después se restauran las tres construcciones que vale la pena tener.
